prompt: A manufacturing company assigns internal project codes that always start with "PRJ-" followed by six digits. New codes are created every day and there is no central list of them. The security team must detect these codes in documents and email so that DLP policies can act on them. What should the administrator create?

options.text: A document fingerprint based on a sample project document
A custom trainable classifier seeded with project documents
A custom sensitive information type that uses a regular expression as the primary element
An exact data match (EDM) sensitive information type built from a table of project codes

explanation: A custom sensitive information type with a regular expression primary element detects a predictable pattern such as PRJ- followed by six digits, wherever it appears. A document fingerprint detects documents created from a specific form, not a pattern inside arbitrary text. A custom trainable classifier recognises categories of documents from examples, not short identifiers. An EDM sensitive information type needs a source table of exact values, which the company does not have because codes are created constantly with no central list.

prompt: A legal department wants to detect its contracts wherever they are stored. The contracts follow no consistent template, contain no identifiers with a fixed pattern, and vary widely in wording. The department has several hundred example contracts and many non-contract documents in SharePoint. Which classification method should the administrator use?

options.text: A custom trainable classifier
A keyword dictionary sensitive information type
A document fingerprint
An exact data match (EDM) sensitive information type

explanation: Trainable classifiers suit content that can't easily be identified by pattern matching; they learn a category of content from positive and negative examples. A keyword dictionary depends on specific words appearing, which varied wording makes unreliable. A document fingerprint requires a standard form that every document is created from. EDM matches exact values from a structured source table and is not suited to recognising a type of document.

prompt: A retailer must prevent credit card numbers from being emailed outside the organization. The team wants accurate detection, including checksum validation, with the least administrative effort. What should the administrator use in the DLP policy?

options.text: A custom sensitive information type with a regular expression that matches any 16-digit number
A document fingerprint created from a sample receipt
An exact data match sensitive information type built from the payment database
The built-in Credit Card Number sensitive information type

explanation: Microsoft Purview includes a built-in Credit Card Number sensitive information type that is ready to use, so no custom work is needed. A custom regular expression for any 16-digit number takes more effort and produces more false positives unless validators are added. A document fingerprint detects documents based on a form, not card numbers in any message. An EDM type requires building a schema and hashing and uploading a source table, which is far more effort than the requirement needs.

prompt: A hospital's DLP policy uses the built-in U.S. Social Security Number sensitive information type and generates many false positives from numbers that belong to people who aren't patients. The hospital wants to detect only social security numbers of its own patients, which are stored in a patient database. What should the administrator implement?

options.text: A custom trainable classifier seeded with patient records
An exact data match (EDM) sensitive information type that uses the patient database as its source table
A copy of the built-in U.S. Social Security Number type with a higher confidence level and extra keywords
A document fingerprint created from the patient intake form

explanation: EDM-based classification compares content against exact values in a source table of sensitive data, which results in fewer false positives and detects only the hospital's actual patients. A trainable classifier recognises categories of documents, not specific people's identifiers. Raising the confidence level of a copied built-in type still matches any valid-looking SSN, patient or not. A document fingerprint only detects documents based on the intake form and would miss SSNs in other content.

prompt: An administrator is preparing to hash and upload a sensitive information source table for an exact data match sensitive information type. The account that runs the EDM Upload Agent must be a member of which security group?

options.text: Compliance Data Administrators
Information Protection Admins
EDM_DataUploaders
Content Explorer Content viewer

explanation: The work or school account used with the EDM Upload Agent must be added to a security group named EDM_DataUploaders. Compliance data administrator is a Microsoft Entra role and doesn't authorize uploads by itself. Information Protection Admins is a Purview role group for managing information protection, not the upload group the agent checks. Content Explorer Content viewer grants the ability to view item contents in Content explorer, unrelated to EDM uploads.

prompt: A company follows the recommended two-computer method for an exact data match sensitive information type. The clear-text source table is on a secure computer that has no internet connection. Which EDM Upload Agent command should the administrator run on the secure computer?

options.text: EdmUploadAgent.exe /UploadData
EdmUploadAgent.exe /UploadHash
EdmUploadAgent.exe /GetSession
EdmUploadAgent.exe /CreateHash

explanation: On the secure computer, /CreateHash hashes the source table with a salt and outputs EdmHash and EdmSalt files, which are then copied to an internet-connected computer. /UploadData hashes and uploads in one step, so it needs a direct connection to the tenant and is the single-computer method. /UploadHash runs on the internet-connected computer to upload the hash file. /GetSession lists uploads to a data store and doesn't hash anything.

prompt: An exact data match sensitive information type uses a customer account number as its primary element. The administrator wants street addresses such as "1432 Lincoln Road" in the source table to count as corroborative evidence. How should the address field be configured in the EDM schema?

options.text: As a second primary element
As a keyword dictionary
As a multi-token field
As an ignored delimiter field

explanation: Multi-token matching lets EDM compare hashes of consecutive words in content with corroborative fields that contain more than one word, such as names and addresses, when the field is marked as multi-token in the schema. An EDM SIT defines one primary element, and the account number already fills that role. A keyword dictionary is a static list of terms and wouldn't use the hashed per-customer values. Ignoring delimiters is a configurable match option that changes how a value is compared, not a way to match multi-word values.

prompt: A law firm requires clients to complete a standard blank intellectual property disclosure form. The firm wants a DLP policy to detect completed copies of the form leaving the organization. What should the administrator do first?

options.text: Create a custom trainable classifier using completed forms as seed content
Create an exact data match schema from the form's field names
Create a sensitivity label with a content marking that matches the form
Upload the blank form to create a fingerprint-based sensitive information type

explanation: Document fingerprinting converts a standard form into a sensitive information type that detects documents created from that form, and uploading the empty form gives the most effective fingerprint. A trainable classifier needs at least 50 positive and 150 negative samples and is meant for broad categories of content rather than one form. EDM matches values from a source table of data, not the wording of a form. A content marking adds text to labeled items and does not detect unlabeled forms.

prompt: A fingerprint-based sensitive information type created from an HR form detects most completed forms, but some completed forms are never detected. Which two characteristics would prevent the undetected files from matching the fingerprint? (Choose two.)

options.text: The files are password protected
The files are stored in OneDrive rather than SharePoint
The files contain additional text that employees typed into the form fields
The files are scanned copies that contain only images
The files are saved in .docx format

explanation: Document fingerprinting doesn't detect sensitive information in password-protected files or in files that contain images only. OneDrive is a supported DLP location for fingerprint SITs. Extra text typed into the fields is expected, because people fill out the form while keeping its original words. The .docx format is a normal text-based file type that fingerprints work with.

prompt: A company has a confidential pricing template. It wants a fingerprint-based sensitive information type to report a high confidence match only when a file has exactly the same text as the template, with no deviation. How should the administrator configure the fingerprint?

options.text: Set the high confidence level to Exact
Set the low confidence threshold to 90 percent
Set the medium confidence threshold to 30 percent
Add a keyword list of phrases from the template as a supporting element

explanation: Selecting Exact as the value for the high confidence level makes the fingerprint detect only files with exactly the same text as the template. Partial matching thresholds, such as 90 or 30 percent, still allow files that differ from the template, and 30 percent at medium confidence would be very loose. Fingerprint SITs are configured with confidence thresholds, not keyword-list supporting elements.

prompt: An organization adds a fingerprint-based sensitive information type to a DLP policy scoped to Exchange, SharePoint, and Devices. Detections occur in email and SharePoint, but never on onboarded Windows devices. What should the administrator turn on?

options.text: Optical character recognition for devices
Just-in-time protection
Advanced classification scanning and protection
Device onboarding in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps

explanation: To use document fingerprinting with devices, Advanced classification scanning and protection must be turned on in the endpoint DLP settings. OCR extends detection to text in images, which doesn't explain missing fingerprint matches in text files. Just-in-time protection restricts activity on files that haven't been scanned yet and doesn't enable fingerprint classification. Defender for Cloud Apps doesn't onboard devices for endpoint DLP.

prompt: An administrator is gathering seed content for a new custom trainable classifier. What is the minimum seed content required to train the classifier?

options.text: 10 positive samples and 10 negative samples
50 positive samples and 150 negative samples
200 positive samples and no negative samples
500 positive samples and 1,500 negative samples

explanation: Training a custom classifier needs at least 50 positive samples and at least 150 negative samples. Ten of each is well below the minimum. Negative samples are required, so positive samples alone can't train a classifier. 500 positive and 1,500 negative samples are the upper limits, not the minimum.

prompt: An administrator is preparing positive and negative seed content for a custom trainable classifier. Where should the seed content be stored?

options.text: In two folders in the administrator's OneDrive
In the Files tab of a Teams channel
In a single SharePoint folder, with the positive files identified by a file name prefix
In two separate SharePoint folders, each dedicated only to one set of seed content

explanation: Positive and negative seed content must be placed in separate SharePoint folders, each holding only seed content, on a communication site or other SharePoint site type. OneDrive folders and Teams folder types aren't supported for seed content. A single folder mixing both sets doesn't work, because the classifier takes positive and negative examples from separate folder sources.

prompt: A custom trainable classifier was published three months ago and now produces too many false positives. The team has collected a much larger set of positive and negative samples. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Remove the classifier and create a new one using the larger sample sets
Retrain the published classifier with the new samples
Replace the classifier with a keyword dictionary sensitive information type
Convert the classifier into a custom sensitive information type

explanation: Retraining a published custom classifier isn't supported; to improve its accuracy you remove it and start over with larger sample sets. Retraining applies only to classifiers that haven't been published yet. A keyword dictionary depends on fixed terms and loses the example-based detection the classifier was built for. A trainable classifier can't be converted into a sensitive information type.

prompt: An organization has created several custom trainable classifiers. In which Microsoft Purview solution can only the Microsoft-provided pretrained classifiers be used, not the custom classifiers?

options.text: Auto-labeling with sensitivity labels
Auto-apply retention label policies
Communication compliance
Data loss prevention

explanation: Communication compliance supports only the Microsoft-provided pretrained trainable classifiers; custom trainable classifiers aren't supported there. Sensitivity label auto-labeling, auto-apply retention label policies, and DLP can all use custom trainable classifiers as conditions.

prompt: A compliance analyst must open and read the contents of files that matched the Credit Card Number sensitive information type in Content explorer. The analyst can already open the Content explorer page and see the list of items. Which role group should the analyst be added to?

options.text: Content Explorer List viewer
Information Protection Readers
Compliance Data Administrator
Content Explorer Content viewer

explanation: Content Explorer Content viewer grants permission to view the contents of each item in the list, and is also needed to see item names, which can contain sensitive data. Content Explorer List viewer only shows items and their locations in list view. Information Protection Readers and the Compliance data administrator role grant access to the tab but not to the items or their contents.

prompt: A security analyst has the Microsoft Entra Compliance administrator role. The analyst can open Data explorer but can't see any items or their locations. The analyst must see each item and where it is stored, without viewing file contents. What should be done?

options.text: Assign the analyst the Global Administrator role
Add the analyst to the Data Explorer List viewer role group
Add the analyst to the Data Explorer Content viewer role group
Add the analyst to the EDM_DataUploaders security group

explanation: Data Explorer List viewer lets an account see each item and its location in list view, which meets the requirement without granting access to contents. Global Administrator, like Compliance administrator, gives access to the tab but not to the list of items, and breaks least privilege. Data Explorer Content viewer allows viewing item contents, which is more than required. EDM_DataUploaders only authorizes EDM source table uploads.

prompt: An administrator applied a new sensitivity label to a set of files in a SharePoint site yesterday. Content explorer doesn't show the files under the new label yet. Sensitivity labels for SharePoint and OneDrive files are already enabled. What is the most likely explanation?

options.text: Content explorer can take up to 14 days to update counts for files in SharePoint
The label must also be published to the site's owners
The administrator lacks the Content Explorer Content viewer role
Content explorer shows only items that match sensitive information types, not labels

explanation: It can take up to seven days for counts to update in Content explorer, and up to 14 days for files in SharePoint, so a label applied yesterday may not appear yet. Publishing the label to site owners has no effect on how Content explorer reports items that already have it. The Content viewer role controls access to item contents and names, not whether a label's items are counted. Content explorer shows items with sensitivity labels and retention labels as well as sensitive information types.

prompt: A company starts using sensitivity labels on Office files stored in SharePoint and OneDrive. Labeled files in Exchange appear in Content explorer, but files in SharePoint and OneDrive never appear, even after several weeks. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: OCR scanning hasnt been configured for the SharePoint and OneDrive locations
The files also have retention labels applied by an auto-apply policy
Sensitivity labels for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive havent been enabled
Content explorer doesnt report items stored in OneDrive accounts

explanation: Sensitivity labels must be enabled for files in SharePoint and OneDrive for the corresponding data to surface in data classification views such as Content explorer. OCR only extends detection to images and doesn't affect labeled Office files. Retention labels don't stop sensitivity labels from being reported; Content explorer shows both. OneDrive is a supported location in Content explorer.

prompt: A company wants DLP policies to detect sensitive information in scanned images and image-only PDFs in Exchange and SharePoint. The tenant has no Azure subscription. What must happen before the compliance administrator can configure OCR scanning?

options.text: An Azure pay-as-you-go subscription linked through Syntex billing
A Microsoft Purview Information Protection scanner must be installed
A custom trainable classifier must be trained on image files
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps must be connected to Microsoft 365

explanation: OCR is an optional pay-as-you-go feature: a Global admin must set up an Azure pay-as-you-go subscription and add it through Microsoft Syntex billing before the compliance administrator configures OCR. The information protection scanner is for on-premises file shares, not OCR in Microsoft 365. Custom trainable classifiers support only text-based seed files, and OCR needs no separate classifiers. Defender for Cloud Apps isn't a prerequisite for Purview OCR.

prompt: OCR has been configured in Microsoft Purview with Exchange and SharePoint selected as locations. An existing DLP policy uses the Credit Card Number sensitive information type. What else must the administrator do for the policy to detect credit card numbers in images?

options.text: Create a copy of the Credit Card Number type that is enabled for images
Add a condition that detects image file extensions to the DLP rule
Train a custom classifier with images that contain card numbers
Nothing; existing sensitive information types also scan images

explanation: OCR is configured at tenant level, and existing sensitive information types, EDM types, trainable classifiers and fingerprints then scan images as well as text, so existing policies apply to images without changes. There is no image-enabled copy of a sensitive information type. Adding a file extension condition would restrict the rule rather than enable OCR. Custom classifiers can't be trained on image files.

prompt: A company has configured OCR for Exchange. To control pay-as-you-go costs, it wants OCR to scan images only in email sent to recipients outside the organization, not in incoming or internal mail. Which OCR setting should the administrator configure?

options.text: Change the sender scope from All sender groups to a group that contains only external senders
Select the Exchange-only advanced setting that limits OCR to mail sent outside the organization
Exclude internal domains in the endpoint DLP file path exclusions
Remove Exchange from the OCR locations and add a mail flow rule

explanation: The OCR settings include an advanced option for Exchange only that restricts OCR to mail sent outside the organization; with it selected, incoming mail and internal communications aren't scanned. Sender groups contain internal users, so changing the sender scope can exclude incoming mail but still scans internal mail. Endpoint file path exclusions apply to folders on devices, not email. Removing Exchange from the OCR locations stops all image scanning in email, and a mail flow rule doesn't perform OCR.

prompt: An administrator needs a sensitive information type that behaves like the built-in U.S. Bank Account Number type but with an extra keyword list that the company uses. The administrator wants to change as little as possible. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Edit the built-in U.S. Bank Account Number type and add the keyword list
Create an exact data match sensitive information type from bank account records
Copy the built-in type, then edit the copy to add the keyword list
Create a document fingerprint from a bank statement

explanation: Purview lets you copy an existing sensitive information type and then edit the copy's patterns and supporting elements, which keeps the built-in logic while adding the keywords. Built-in sensitive information types can't be edited directly. EDM requires a schema and a source table of account data, which is far more work than the requirement. A fingerprint detects documents based on a form, not bank account numbers in any content.

prompt: An administrator creates a custom sensitive information type with the regular expression ^EMP[0-9]{5}$ to detect employee numbers. Testing shows that it misses employee numbers that appear in the middle of documents. What should the administrator change?

options.text: Remove the ^ and $ positional anchors from the regular expression
Increase the character proximity of the pattern to 5,000 characters
Change the recommended confidence level to Low
Add a checksum validator to the regular expression

explanation: Custom SIT regular expressions must not use positional anchors such as ^ and $, because there is no guarantee where scanned content starts and ends, so anchored patterns miss values inside the text. Character proximity controls the distance to supporting elements, not whether the primary pattern matches. Lowering the confidence level doesn't fix a pattern that fails to match. A checksum validator adds a further check and would make matching stricter, not looser.

prompt: A new custom sensitive information type is created and added to a DLP policy for SharePoint. New files that contain the information are detected, but existing files in a document library that haven't changed are not. What should the administrator do so that the existing files are identified?

options.text: Delete and recreate the DLP policy
Request a recrawl and reindex of the document library
Increase the custom type's confidence level to High
Enable optical character recognition for SharePoint

explanation: Microsoft 365 uses the search crawler to classify content in SharePoint and OneDrive, so existing content must be recrawled for a new custom type to be identified; you can manually request a recrawl of a site collection, list or library. Recreating the DLP policy doesn't reclassify unchanged content. Raising the confidence level would reduce matches rather than add them. OCR only extracts text from images and doesn't reclassify existing text files.

prompt: A company wants a team member to create and manage sensitivity labels and label policies. Following least privilege, the team member must not receive broader compliance permissions. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Add the team member to the Compliance Administrator role group
Create a role group with the Sensitivity Label Administrator role and add the team member
Create a role group that contains the Sensitivity Label Reader role and add the team member
Assign the team member the Global Administrator role

explanation: A custom role group with the Sensitivity Label Administrator role grants the permissions to create and configure sensitivity labels and their policies without unrelated compliance permissions. The Compliance Administrator role group works but grants far more than labeling. Sensitivity Label Reader is read-only and can't create labels. Global Administrator is the opposite of least privilege.

prompt: A multinational company has configured Microsoft Entra administrative units for each country. A regional administrator in the Information Protection Admins role group must manage sensitivity label policies only for users in France. What should be configured?

options.text: A separate Microsoft Purview tenant for the French subsidiary
A sensitivity label with the Groups & sites scope for France
A label policy that excludes all users outside France by listing them individually
Assign the France administrative unit to the administrator in the role group

explanation: Members of the role groups used with Information Protection can be assigned administrative units, which restricts them to managing just the users in those units, and policies they create are scoped to those units. A separate tenant is unnecessary and would split the organization's labels. A Groups & sites label controls containers and has nothing to do with administrative scope. Listing users individually doesn't restrict what the administrator can manage, and it breaks as users join.

prompt: A company wants a sensitivity label that users can apply only to Teams, Microsoft 365 groups, and SharePoint sites. The label must not appear in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or Outlook. How should the label's scope be configured?

options.text: Select only the Groups & sites scope
Select the Files & other data assets and Groups & sites scopes
Select the Emails and Meetings scopes
Select the Files & other data assets scope and exclude email

explanation: When only the Groups & sites scope is selected, the label isn't displayed in Office apps and can't be applied to files and emails, but it can be applied to containers. Adding the Files & other data assets scope makes the label available in Office apps. The Emails and Meetings scopes make the label available in Outlook and Teams meetings and don't include containers. A Files-only scope makes the label appear in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint and doesn't cover containers.

prompt: An administrator creates a new sensitivity label, but the protection settings for groups and sites are visible and can't be configured. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Assign the administrator the Sensitivity Label Reader role in the Microsoft Purview portal
Enable sensitivity labels for Office files stored in SharePoint and OneDrive
Enable label support for groups in Microsoft Entra ID, then run Execute-AzureAdLabelSync
Publish the label to all users and wait 24 hours for the settings to replicate

explanation: Container support is enabled once by turning on sensitivity label support for Microsoft 365 groups in Microsoft Entra ID (the EnableMIPLabels setting) and then synchronizing labels with Execute-AzureAdLabelSync; until then, the group and site settings are visible but can't be configured. Sensitivity Label Reader is read-only and grants no extra configuration. Enabling labels for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive affects files, not container settings. Publishing the label doesn't unlock settings that depend on container support.

prompt: A label policy requires users to justify removing a label or changing it to a lower classification. Users who change Highly Confidential to General are not prompted, but users who change General to Highly Confidential are. Highly Confidential is at the top of the Labels list and General is at the bottom. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Turn on mandatory labeling in the label policy for all users
Move the label policy to a higher order number in the list
Convert Highly Confidential into a sublabel of General
Move Highly Confidential to the bottom of the Labels list

explanation: Label order sets priority: the most restrictive label should be at the bottom of the list, and the justification setting uses this order to decide what counts as a lower classification. Because the order is reversed, the prompts are reversed. Mandatory labeling forces users to apply a label but doesn't change what is treated as a downgrade. Label policy order resolves conflicting settings between policies, not label priority. Making Highly Confidential a sublabel of General would give both the same priority, so no justification would be needed for that change.

prompt: An administrator wants to create a sensitivity label that can be applied to calendar events, Teams meeting options, and Teams chat. Which scopes must be selected for the label?

options.text: Meetings, Emails, and Groups & sites, without Files
Files & other data assets, Emails, and Meetings
Meetings and Files & other data assets
Emails and Meetings

explanation: The Meetings scope covers calendar events, Teams meeting options, and Teams chat, and it requires the Files & other data assets and Emails scopes to be selected as well. Groups & sites applies to containers and isn't required for meetings. Meetings on its own, or Meetings with only Emails, doesn't meet the requirement that Files & other data assets also be selected.

prompt: Users must be able to send encrypted email to customers who use personal email accounts such as Gmail. Recipients must not be able to forward, print, or copy the message. The sender, not the administrator, decides who the recipients are. How should the sensitivity label's encryption be configured?

options.text: Let users assign permissions, and in Outlook enforce the Do Not Forward option
Assign permissions now, and grant Viewer permissions to all users and groups in the organization
Let users assign permissions, and in Outlook enforce the Encrypt-Only option
Assign permissions now, and set user access to content to expire after 7 days

explanation: With Let users assign permissions and the Do Not Forward option, the sender picks the recipients and recipients can't forward, print, or copy the email. Granting permissions to all users in the organization would exclude Gmail recipients. Encrypt-Only lets recipients copy, print, and forward the message; it only stops them removing protection. An expiry setting limits how long content can be opened but doesn't stop forwarding or printing, and assigning permissions now means the administrator, not the sender, chooses who has access.

prompt: A company wants email to partners to stay encrypted but places no other restrictions on recipients. Recipients must be able to copy, print, and forward the message, but must not be able to remove the protection. Which encryption option should the sensitivity label use in Outlook?

options.text: Do Not Forward
Double Key Encryption
Encrypt-Only
Assign permissions now with the Reviewer permission level

explanation: Encrypt-Only gives recipients all usage rights except Save As, Export, and Full Control, so they can copy, print, and forward but can't remove protection. Do Not Forward prevents forwarding, printing, and copying. Double Key Encryption is for highly sensitive content where Microsoft must not be able to decrypt it, and it adds infrastructure without meeting the stated need. Reviewer permissions assigned by the administrator fix the users who have access and don't suit ad hoc partner email.

prompt: A Confidential sensitivity label is used for both documents and email. The company wants visible text identifying the content as Confidential to appear on documents and on email messages. Which content marking should the administrator configure?

options.text: A watermark only
A header or footer
Dynamic watermarking
A custom help link in the label policy

explanation: Headers and footers can be applied to email, meeting invites, and documents. Watermarks can be applied to documents and Loop components but not to email or meeting invites. Dynamic watermarking is a protective watermark for labels that apply encryption and doesn't mark email. A custom help link points users to guidance and doesn't mark content.

prompt: A company shares project documents with contractors. Contractors must lose the ability to open a labeled document 30 days after the label is applied, regardless of where the file is stored. Which sensitivity label encryption setting should the administrator configure?

options.text: Allow offline access to the content for 30 days
Require users to apply a label to their documents
Set the label as the default label for new documents
Set user access to content to expire after 30 days

explanation: The encryption setting that lets access to labeled content expire on a date or a number of days after the label is applied stops users opening the item after that time. Offline access controls how long a use license lets users open content without reauthenticating, not when access ends. Mandatory labeling and a default label control whether and which label is applied, not how long access lasts.

prompt: A defense contractor must protect a small set of highly sensitive documents so that Microsoft can't decrypt them, even under legal compulsion. The company runs its own key service. Which sensitivity label encryption option meets the requirement?

options.text: Double Key Encryption
Encrypt-Only
Assign permissions now with any authenticated users
Let users assign permissions in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint

explanation: Double Key Encryption protects content with two keys, one of which is held by the customer's own Double Key Encryption service, so Microsoft can't decrypt the content alone; it's intended for the most sensitive data. Encrypt-Only, any authenticated users, and user-assigned permissions all use standard Azure Rights Management protection without a second customer-held key, so they don't meet the requirement. A DKE label must be selected only after the DKE service is configured, and it can't be edited after it's saved.

prompt: An administrator created a new sensitivity label named Finance Restricted an hour ago. Members of the finance group report that the label doesn't appear in Word or Outlook. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The label's scope includes Groups & sites in addition to files and emails
The finance users must first be assigned the Sensitivity Label Reader role
The label hasn't been published to the finance group in a label policy
The label must be used in an auto-labeling policy before users can see it

explanation: Sensitivity labels must be published in a label policy to users or groups before apps display them, and changes can take up to 24 hours to replicate. A label scoped to Groups & sites as well as files and email still appears in Office apps. Users don't need admin roles to apply labels; those roles are only for configuring labels and policies. Auto-labeling is optional and doesn't make a label visible to users.

prompt: A user is included in two sensitivity label policies. The All Users policy has order number 0 and sets General as the default label for documents. The Legal policy has order number 2 and sets Confidential as the default label for documents. Which default label does the user get for new documents?

options.text: General, because the All Users policy has the lowest order number
Confidential, because the Legal policy has the higher order number
No default label, because the policies conflict
Whichever policy was created most recently

explanation: When a user is assigned several label policies and their settings conflict, the setting from the policy with the highest priority, meaning the highest order number, is applied. The Legal policy has order number 2, so Confidential is the default. The lowest order number is the lowest priority. Conflicts don't cancel the setting, and creation date has no effect on precedence.

prompt: A company requires every document and email to carry a sensitivity label before it is saved or sent. Users who handle low-sensitivity content complain that they are constantly prompted to choose a label. Which two label policy settings together meet the requirement while reducing prompts? (Choose two.)

options.text: Require users to apply a label to their email and documents
Require a justification to remove a label or lower its classification
Provide users with a link to a custom help page
Apply a default label, such as General, to documents and email
Assign permissions now with an expiry date

explanation: Mandatory labeling makes sure a label is applied before users save files or send email, and setting a default label means most items already have a label, so users aren't prompted repeatedly. Requiring justification only applies when users remove or downgrade a label. A custom help link provides guidance but doesn't apply labels. Encryption with an expiry date is a label setting, not a label policy setting, and doesn't reduce prompts.

prompt: Users are unsure which sensitivity label to choose. The company has written an internal guide and wants users to reach it from the Sensitivity button in Office apps. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: A tooltip in each label that includes the URL of the internal guide
A header content marking that displays the URL of the internal guide
A recommended label setting with a customized policy tip message
The label policy setting for a link to a custom help page

explanation: The label policy setting that provides users with a link to a custom help page adds a Learn More option to the Sensitivity button that opens the internal guide. A tooltip describes a single label and may be truncated in some apps. A header marking adds text to labeled content rather than giving users help when choosing. A recommended label shows a policy tip for specific content and isn't a general help link.

prompt: A company wants existing Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files stored in specific SharePoint sites that contain passport numbers to be labeled Confidential automatically. Users must not be involved and the labeling must not depend on their Office app versions. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: An auto-labeling policy for the SharePoint sites that applies the Confidential label
The auto-labeling for files and emails setting in the Confidential label, set to automatically apply the label
A label policy with Confidential as the default label for documents
A DLP policy that blocks sharing of files that contain passport numbers

explanation: Service-side auto-labeling policies label content already saved in SharePoint or OneDrive without user involvement and independently of app versions. The label's auto-labeling setting runs client-side in Office apps when users edit content, so it doesn't label files at rest. A default label applies to new unlabeled documents that users create, not to existing files that contain passport numbers. A DLP policy restricts sharing but doesn't apply a label.

prompt: An administrator creates an auto-labeling policy for OneDrive. The policy must start labeling files without waiting for an administrator to turn it on manually after simulation, unless someone changes it. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Skip the simulation and create the auto-labeling policy directly in enforcement mode
Set the auto-labeling policy's priority to 0 so that it runs first
Turn the policy on automatically if it isn't edited for 7 days after simulation
Publish the label to all users with mandatory labeling turned on

explanation: Auto-labeling policies must complete at least one simulation before they can label content, and when you create a policy you can choose to turn it on automatically if it isn't edited for 7 days after simulation. Simulation can't be skipped. Policy priority doesn't change simulation behaviour. Mandatory labeling in a label policy affects users in Office apps, not the auto-labeling policy.

prompt: An auto-labeling policy applies the Confidential label to SharePoint files that contain bank account numbers. After enforcement, several matching files still have the Highly Confidential label that users applied manually. Highly Confidential has higher priority than Confidential. What explains this result?

options.text: The policy is still in simulation mode
Auto-labeling never replaces a manually applied label with higher priority
The files exceed the daily auto-labeling limit and will be relabeled later
Auto-labeling policies don't support Excel files

explanation: An auto-labeling policy never replaces a manually applied label that has higher priority, so files manually labeled Highly Confidential keep that label. A policy still in simulation wouldn't have labeled any files, yet other files have been labeled. The daily throughput limit delays processing but wouldn't replace a higher-priority manual label later. Auto-labeling for SharePoint and OneDrive supports Word, PowerPoint, and Excel files and PDFs.

prompt: An auto-labeling policy is configured for the Exchange location. The compliance team expects it to label messages that were already stored in user mailboxes before the policy was enabled, but those messages remain unlabeled. Why?

options.text: Exchange auto-labeling requires a trainable classifier
The label applies encryption, which Exchange auto-labeling doesn't support
The policy needs the Sensitivity Label Administrator role assigned to each mailbox
Exchange auto-labeling evaluates email in transit, not mailboxes at rest

explanation: For Exchange, auto-labeling policies evaluate email in transit, when it is sent or received; mailboxes at rest aren't included. Trainable classifiers are optional conditions, not a requirement. Exchange-only auto-labeling policies can apply labels with encryption, including Assign permissions now, Do Not Forward, and Encrypt-Only. Roles are assigned to administrators, not to mailboxes.

prompt: A company wants Word users who type credit card numbers into a document to see a prompt suggesting the Confidential label, which they can accept or dismiss. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: The Confidential label's own auto-labeling setting, set to recommend the label
An auto-labeling policy for SharePoint and OneDrive that applies the Confidential label
A label policy that makes Confidential the default label for documents
A DLP policy tip for credit card numbers in SharePoint

explanation: The label's auto-labeling setting for files and emails runs client-side in Office apps and can recommend a label, which the user accepts or rejects. Service-side auto-labeling policies don't make recommendations and don't involve the user. A default label is applied to all new unlabeled documents regardless of content. A DLP policy tip warns about policy matches but doesn't recommend a sensitivity label.

prompt: A sensitivity label for SharePoint sites is configured to block access from unmanaged devices. After the label is applied to a site, users can still open and download files from unmanaged devices. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The label's scope doesn't include Files & other data assets
Users haven't been required to provide a justification for label changes
The required Conditional Access app-enforced restrictions aren't configured
Sensitivity labels for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive aren't enabled

explanation: The unmanaged devices setting depends on Microsoft Entra Conditional Access and the SharePoint app-enforced restrictions policy; if that policy isn't configured, the label setting has no effect. The Files scope controls whether the label can be applied to items and isn't required for site settings. Justification applies to users changing labels. Enabling labels for Office files in SharePoint lets users label documents and doesn't enforce device restrictions on a site.

prompt: A team is labeled Highly Confidential, which applies encryption and a watermark when it is applied to documents. A manager expects every document uploaded to the team's SharePoint site to be encrypted and watermarked, but the documents have no protection. What explains this?

options.text: The team's privacy setting is Public, so the label settings are ignored
Items in a labeled container don't inherit the container's label
The label policy for the team owners has a lower order number than other policies
Encryption by sensitivity labels isn't supported for files stored in SharePoint

explanation: Items in labeled containers don't inherit the container label, so item-level settings such as encryption and content markings aren't applied to them; a separate approach, such as a default sensitivity label for the document library, is needed to label the files. The privacy setting controls who can join the container, not file protection. Label policy order resolves conflicting policy settings and doesn't apply labels to files. SharePoint supports files encrypted by sensitivity labels.

prompt: Sensitivity labels are published to all users, but Power BI report authors can't see or apply labels to reports and semantic models in the Power BI service. What should the Fabric administrator do?

options.text: Add the Power BI service as a location in an auto-labeling policy
Enable the Groups & sites scope on each of the published labels
Assign each of the report authors the Sensitivity Label Administrator role
Turn on the Allow users to apply sensitivity labels for content tenant setting

explanation: Sensitivity labels must be enabled for Fabric and Power BI through the Information protection tenant setting Allow users to apply sensitivity labels for content in the admin portal, optionally scoped to security groups. An auto-labeling policy isn't how Power BI labeling is enabled. The Groups & sites scope is for containers such as Teams and SharePoint sites. Applying labels doesn't require an administrative role.

prompt: A company stores contracts in Box and has connected Box to Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps. It wants files in Box that match a contract pattern to be labeled Confidential automatically. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: A Defender for Cloud Apps file policy with the Apply sensitivity label action
An auto-labeling policy in Microsoft Purview that includes Box as a location for the label
A label policy published to the Box service account
A session policy that blocks downloads from Box

explanation: Defender for Cloud Apps can apply Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels to files in connected apps, including Box, by using a file policy whose governance action is Apply sensitivity label. Purview auto-labeling policies cover Exchange, SharePoint, and OneDrive, not Box. Publishing a label to a service account doesn't label files in Box. A session policy controls user sessions in real time and doesn't label stored files.

prompt: An administrator wants to use a Defender for Cloud Apps file policy to apply a sensitivity label to files in Google Workspace, but the label isn't listed in the governance action. The label is published in a label policy. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The label applies a header content marking
The label uses Assign permissions now for all users in the organization
The label's scope includes only Groups & sites
The label policy has mandatory labeling turned on

explanation: For Defender for Cloud Apps to recognize a sensitivity label, the label's scope in Purview must include at least files and emails, so a label scoped only to Groups & sites isn't available. Content markings don't stop a label from being used. Assigning permissions to all users in the organization is one of the configurations Defender for Cloud Apps needs to read label information. Mandatory labeling affects users in apps and doesn't hide labels from Defender for Cloud Apps.

prompt: Engineers on Windows 11 computers need to apply sensitivity labels to PDF files, images, and Visio drawings directly from File Explorer, without opening an Office app. What should the administrator deploy?

options.text: The sensitivity labels built into Microsoft 365 Apps
A Defender for Cloud Apps file policy
An auto-labeling policy for OneDrive
The Microsoft Purview Information Protection client

explanation: The Microsoft Purview Information Protection client includes the file labeler that applies sensitivity labels and encryption from File Explorer, and supports a wider range of file types. Built-in labeling works inside Office apps rather than File Explorer. A Defender for Cloud Apps file policy labels files in connected cloud apps, not local files chosen by users. An auto-labeling policy labels files at rest in OneDrive automatically and doesn't let users label files from File Explorer.

prompt: An administrator must deploy the Microsoft Purview Information Protection client to 3,000 managed Windows computers by using Microsoft Intune. Which installer should the administrator use?

options.text: The .msi version of the client
The Information Protection add-in for Office
The EDM Upload Agent
The information protection scanner package with Install-Scanner

explanation: For central deployment, Microsoft provides an .msi version of the client, which can be added as an app in Microsoft Intune and run with /quiet. There's no Office add-in with this client, because built-in labeling in Office replaces it. The EDM Upload Agent hashes and uploads exact data match tables. Install-Scanner installs the scanner service on a server, not the client on user computers.

prompt: A company has some Windows computers that can't connect to the internet. It wants users on those computers to apply sensitivity labels with the Microsoft Purview Information Protection client by copying exported policy files to them. Which labels can be used on the disconnected computers?

options.text: Only labels that apply Double Key Encryption
Only labels that let users assign permissions
Only labels that don't apply encryption
Any published label, including labels that apply encryption

explanation: The client needs an active internet connection to apply encryption, so the disconnected computers solution is supported only for labels that don't apply encryption. Double Key Encryption and user-assigned permissions both apply encryption and so need connectivity. Encrypting labels can't be used on a computer that can't reach the service.

prompt: An organization uses Group Policy to deploy the Microsoft Purview Information Protection client silently to computers that still have the Azure Information Protection unified labeling client installed. The silent installations fail. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Install the client again with the PowerShellOnly=true option
Set the AllowMajorVersionUpgrade registry value to 1, or remove the old client first
Run Execute-AzureAdLabelSync in Security & Compliance PowerShell before deployment
Enable the AIP add-in for Office on each computer before deployment

explanation: For a non-interactive installation when the Azure Information Protection client is present, you must either uninstall the older client or create the AllowMajorVersionUpgrade DWORD set to 1, which allows the upgrade and removes the AIP Office add-in. PowerShellOnly=true installs only the cmdlets and doesn't solve the upgrade block. Execute-AzureAdLabelSync synchronizes labels for containers. The AIP Office add-in is what the upgrade removes, so enabling it doesn't help.

prompt: A user tries to apply a sensitivity label named General, which applies no encryption, to a folder of .txt files by using the Microsoft Purview Information Protection client. The files aren't labeled. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: The .txt file type doesn't support sensitivity labels without encryption
The user isn't a member of the Information Protection Admins role group
The General label is scoped to Groups & sites
The files must be uploaded to SharePoint first

explanation: The .txt file type isn't in the list of file types that can be labeled without encryption, so a label without encryption can't be applied; a label that applies encryption could protect it as .ptxt. Users don't need an admin role group to apply labels. A Groups & sites-only label wouldn't appear in the file labeler at all, while the user could select General. The client labels local files and doesn't require them to be in SharePoint.

prompt: A user applies a sensitivity label that encrypts content for the Finance group to accounts.zip by using the Microsoft Purview Information Protection client. The file is renamed accounts.zip.pfile. Which statement describes the protection on the file?

options.text: Finance members can open it, and usage rights such as no-print are enforced in every app
Anyone can open it, but the label is recorded in the audit log
It is protected with native encryption, and the file becomes read-only
Only authorized users can open it, but usage rights aren't enforced after it opens

explanation: File types that don't support native encryption get generic encryption, which wraps the file as a .pfile and requires authentication, so only authorized users can open it; usage rights are displayed but not enforced. Enforced usage rights apply only to native encryption. Generic encryption still blocks unauthorized users, so the file isn't open to everyone. Native encryption applies to types such as Office files, PDF, text, and images, not .zip.

prompt: An administrator must label thousands of existing files in a local folder by inspecting their contents and applying labels according to each label's automatic labeling conditions. The administrator wants to use the Microsoft Purview Information Protection client from a script. Which cmdlet should be used?

options.text: Set-Label in Security & Compliance PowerShell
Set-FileLabel with the -Autolabel parameter
Set-LabelPolicy with a PowerShell advanced setting
Start-ScannerDiagnostics on the local computer

explanation: Set-FileLabel with -Autolabel from the Purview Information Protection PowerShell module inspects file contents and applies labels according to their conditions. Set-Label and Set-LabelPolicy are Security & Compliance PowerShell cmdlets for configuring labels and label policies, not for labeling files. Start-ScannerDiagnostics troubleshoots the scanner and doesn't label files.

prompt: After users start encrypting .jpg and .png files with a sensitivity label through the Microsoft Purview Information Protection client, a web proxy that filters by file name extension starts blocking the files. What is the cause?

options.text: Encrypted images are converted to PDF files by the client
Native encryption changes the extensions, such as .jpg to .pjpg
The client compresses encrypted images into .zip archives
The client deletes the original file and stores it in OneDrive

explanation: When the client natively encrypts file types such as images and text files, it changes the extension, for example to .pjpg or .ppng, and the files become read-only; network devices that act on extensions might need to be reconfigured. Images aren't converted to PDF. The client doesn't compress files into archives; it encrypts them in place. The client encrypts files in place and doesn't move them to OneDrive.

prompt: A user receives a file named results.ptxt from a colleague. The file was encrypted by a sensitivity label through the Microsoft Purview Information Protection client. Which component should the user use to read it on Windows?

options.text: Microsoft Purview Information Protection viewer
The Information Protection scanner
The EDM Upload Agent
Microsoft Edge with the Office Online extension

explanation: The information protection viewer, part of the Purview Information Protection client, opens encrypted files such as protected text and image files and enforces their usage rights. The scanner discovers and labels files in data stores and isn't for reading files. The EDM Upload Agent uploads hashed data for EDM. Edge can open protected PDFs, but it isn't the tool for .ptxt files.

prompt: A company must discover, label, and encrypt existing files that contain sensitive data on on-premises SMB file shares and SharePoint Server document libraries. What should the administrator deploy?

options.text: An auto-labeling policy for SharePoint and OneDrive
Endpoint DLP on the file servers
The Microsoft Purview Information Protection scanner
A Defender for Cloud Apps file policy

explanation: The information protection scanner runs as a service on Windows Server and discovers, classifies, and protects files on network shares and SharePoint Server libraries by using sensitivity labels. Auto-labeling policies cover SharePoint and OneDrive in Microsoft 365, not on-premises data stores. Endpoint DLP monitors and restricts user activity on devices rather than bulk labeling file shares. Defender for Cloud Apps file policies apply to connected cloud apps.

prompt: Before labeling anything, a company wants the Microsoft Purview Information Protection scanner to report which files on its file shares would be labeled. How should the content scan job be configured?

options.text: Set Relabel files to On
Set Enable DLP rules to On
Set Default label to a custom label for all files
Set Enforce sensitivity labeling policy to Off

explanation: With Enforce sensitivity labeling policy set to Off, the scanner runs in discovery mode and produces reports about what would happen without labeling files. Relabel files lets the scanner change existing labels, which changes files. Enable DLP rules applies DLP policy rules and needs a configured DLP policy. A custom default label tells the scanner which label to apply and does nothing to stop labeling.

prompt: An administrator is preparing a Windows Server computer to run the Microsoft Purview Information Protection scanner. The Install-Scanner cmdlet will be run with the -Cluster parameter. What else must be available for the installation?

options.text: A Microsoft Defender for Endpoint onboarding package
A SQL Server instance where the scanner database can be created
An Azure pay-as-you-go subscription linked through Microsoft Syntex
A security group named EDM_DataUploaders

explanation: Install-Scanner requires a SQL Server instance (default, named, or SQL Server Express) where it creates the scanner database, along with the scanner cluster name. Defender for Endpoint onboarding is for endpoint DLP and isn't a scanner prerequisite. Pay-as-you-go billing through Syntex is for OCR. EDM_DataUploaders is used for exact data match uploads.

prompt: The Microsoft Purview Information Protection scanner is installed and must authenticate to Microsoft Entra ID non-interactively when it runs as a service. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Register a Microsoft Entra app and run Set-Authentication with its details
Run Execute-AzureAdLabelSync in PowerShell on the scanner server
Add the scanner service account to the Content Explorer Content viewer role group
Run EdmUploadAgent.exe /Authorize on the scanner server as an admin

explanation: The scanner gets a Microsoft Entra token by using an app registration: you run Set-Authentication with the app ID, secret (or certificate), tenant ID, and a delegated user account. Execute-AzureAdLabelSync synchronizes labels for containers. Content Explorer role groups control access to classified items in the portal. EdmUploadAgent.exe /Authorize authorizes the EDM Upload Agent, not the scanner.

prompt: A company wants the Microsoft Purview Information Protection scanner to apply the General label to every file in a repository, including files that already have a different label. How should the content scan job be configured?

options.text: Default label set to Policy default, with Relabel files set to Off
Default label set to None, with Enforce sensitivity labeling policy set to Off
Custom default label of General, Relabel files On, and Enforce default label selected
Treat recommended labeling as automatic, with Enable DLP policy rules set to On

explanation: Selecting a custom default label of General, turning on Relabel files, and selecting Enforce default label makes the scanner apply that label to all files, even those already labeled. Policy default with Relabel files off leaves existing labels in place. Turning enforcement off puts the scanner in discovery mode, so nothing is labeled. Treating recommended labels as automatic and enabling DLP rules don't force one label on every file.

prompt: By default, the Microsoft Purview Information Protection scanner encrypts only Office files and PDF files. A company wants it to also encrypt .xml and .tiff files when a label with encryption is applied. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Add .xml and .tiff to the File types to scan list with the Exclude option
Run Set-ScannerContentScan -Enforce Off on the scanner server
Enable optical character recognition for the repository location
Set the PFileSupportedExtensions advanced setting on the scanner's label policy

explanation: To change which file types the scanner protects, specify the PFileSupportedExtensions PowerShell advanced setting on the label policy that applies to the scanner's account, for example with Set-LabelPolicy. Adding the extensions to an exclusion list stops the scanner inspecting them. Setting Enforce to Off puts the scanner in discovery mode. OCR in Purview applies to cloud and endpoint locations and doesn't control scanner encryption.

prompt: A company has created a DLP policy in Microsoft Purview that includes on-premises repositories, and wants the Microsoft Purview Information Protection scanner to apply its rules to files on a file share. What should the administrator configure in the scanner's content scan job?

options.text: Set Enable DLP policy rules to On
Set Relabel files to On
Set Preserve Date modified to Off
Set Default owner to the repository owner

explanation: Setting Enable DLP policy rules to On in the content scan job makes the scanner apply DLP policy rules to the repositories; it should only be turned on when a DLP policy is configured, or the scanner generates errors. Relabel files controls whether existing labels can change. Preserving the modified date is a file setting unrelated to DLP. The repository owner setting is used by DLP actions but doesn't enable DLP rules by itself.

prompt: A company requires that every email sent to recipients outside the organization with the word "Contract" in the subject is encrypted automatically, without users having to choose anything. What should the administrator create?

options.text: A sensitivity label policy that sets a default label for all email
A mail flow rule that applies Office 365 Message Encryption and rights protection
A retention label policy that auto-applies to email containing the word Contract
An outbound spam filter policy in Microsoft Defender for Office 365

explanation: Exchange mail flow rules can encrypt messages that match conditions, such as a subject keyword and recipients outside the organization, by using the Modify the message security action Apply Office 365 Message Encryption and rights protection. A default email label applies to all email, not just matching messages, and users can change it. Retention labels govern how long content is kept, not encryption. Outbound spam policies don't encrypt mail.

prompt: A bank uses Microsoft Purview Message Encryption to send an encrypted statement to a customer who uses a Gmail account. How does the customer read the message?

options.text: The customer must create a Microsoft 365 work account before opening the message
The message is delivered decrypted because Gmail doesn't support message encryption
A wrapper email links to the encrypted message portal, where the customer signs in
The customer must install the Microsoft Purview Information Protection client

explanation: Recipients using Gmail or Yahoo get a wrapper email that directs them to the encrypted message portal, where they can authenticate with a Microsoft account, Gmail, or Yahoo credentials. A Microsoft 365 work account isn't required. Messages aren't sent decrypted to unsupported providers. The information protection client is a Windows labeling tool and isn't needed to read encrypted mail.

prompt: A company's compliance archive can't index encrypted replies that external recipients send back in response to encrypted messages from the organization. The company wants encryption removed from those replies when they arrive. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: A mail flow rule that removes encryption applied by the organization
A sensitivity label that applies the Encrypt-Only option to replies
Run Set-OMEMessageRevocation -Revoke $true for each reply that arrives
A DLP policy that blocks all encrypted messages from external senders

explanation: A mail flow rule with Modify the message security, Remove Office 365 Message Encryption and rights protection applied by the organization, can remove encryption the organization applied, including on replies received from outside. Encrypt-Only adds encryption and doesn't remove it. Revocation stops external recipients reading a message through the portal and doesn't decrypt replies. Blocking encrypted messages would stop legitimate replies arriving.

prompt: An administrator creates an Exchange mail flow rule that applies Microsoft Purview Message Encryption to messages from a specific external partner domain, so that inbound partner email is stored encrypted. Testing shows the partner's messages arrive unencrypted. Why?

options.text: The partner must also enable Microsoft Purview Message Encryption
Encryption by mail flow rule requires Advanced Message Encryption
The rule must use the Do Not Forward template instead of Encrypt
Mail flow rules can't encrypt inbound mail from external senders

explanation: You can't encrypt inbound mail from senders outside your Exchange Online organization; if a rule is set up to do so, the mail is delivered without encryption. The partner's configuration doesn't change this. Basic Message Encryption supports encryption rules for outgoing mail without Advanced Message Encryption. Changing the template doesn't make inbound encryption possible.

prompt: An administrator creates a mail flow rule and selects Apply Office 365 Message Encryption and rights protection, but the list of templates to choose from is empty. What should the administrator check first?

options.text: Whether the rule's condition includes external recipients
Whether Message Encryption has been set up for the tenant
Whether the administrator has the Sensitivity Label Reader role
Whether a custom branding template with an expiry date exists

explanation: The template list includes the default templates and options, such as Encrypt and Do Not Forward, plus custom templates; if it's empty, Microsoft Purview Message Encryption hasn't been set up, which depends on the Azure Rights Management service. Rule conditions don't affect which templates are listed. Sensitivity Label Reader is a read-only labeling role and doesn't control Exchange templates. Custom branding templates are optional and aren't rights management templates.

prompt: A company with Microsoft Purview Advanced Message Encryption wants encrypted email sent to external recipients to become unreadable 14 days after it is sent. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Configure a sensitivity label with offline access set to 14 days
Run Set-OMEMessageRevocation for each message once 14 days have passed
Use New-OMEConfiguration -ExternalMailExpiryInDays 14 in a mail flow rule
Create a retention policy that deletes sent items after 14 days

explanation: With Advanced Message Encryption, you create a custom branding template with New-OMEConfiguration and ExternalMailExpiryInDays (1 to 730 days), then apply it in a mail flow rule; expiration only works with custom branding and for external recipients using the portal. Offline access controls use license caching, not message expiry. Revoking messages one by one is manual and doesn't meet an automatic requirement. Deleting the sender's sent items doesn't affect the recipient's copy.

prompt: A user sent an encrypted message with Advanced Message Encryption to a recipient's Yahoo address by mistake. The message used a custom branding template. As an administrator, how can you revoke the message?

options.text: Check IsRevocable with Get-OMEMessageStatus, then run Set-OMEMessageRevocation
Delete the message from the sender's Sent Items folder in Outlook on the web
Run Remove-DlpSensitiveInformationType with the message ID of the email
Remove the sender's Advanced Message Encryption license so the message expires

explanation: Administrators revoke eligible messages by getting the message ID, for example from message trace, checking IsRevocable with Get-OMEMessageStatus, and running Set-OMEMessageRevocation -Revoke $true; the recipient then sees that the message has been revoked when using the portal. Deleting the sender's copy doesn't affect the recipient. Remove-DlpSensitiveInformationType deletes a sensitive information type. Removing a license doesn't revoke messages already sent.

prompt: A sender tries to revoke an encrypted message sent with Advanced Message Encryption to a partner whose mailbox is in another Microsoft 365 organization and who reads it in Outlook. The message can't be revoked. Why?

options.text: Revocation works only for messages that are more than 7 days old
Revocation requires the sender to use Outlook for Mac rather than Outlook on the web
Only messages encrypted with Double Key Encryption can be revoked by the sender
The partner got the inline Outlook experience, which can't be revoked

explanation: Messages can be revoked only when the recipient received a link-based, branded experience through the encrypted message portal; Microsoft 365 and Microsoft account recipients get an inline experience in supported Outlook clients, which can't be revoked. Revocation has no minimum age. Senders revoke from Outlook on the web, not Outlook for Mac. Double Key Encryption is a sensitivity label option and isn't required for revocation.

prompt: A holding company wants encrypted email from each of its three subsidiaries to show that subsidiary's own logo and text in the notification and encrypted message portal. Which capability is required?

options.text: Basic Microsoft Purview Message Encryption with a single default branding template
Advanced Message Encryption with multiple branding templates
Three separate sensitivity label policies with different custom help links
Three Information Protection scanner clusters

explanation: Advanced Message Encryption lets you create multiple branding templates and choose which one applies through mail flow rules, so each subsidiary can have its own branding. Without Advanced Message Encryption you're limited to a single branding template. Custom help links in label policies don't brand encrypted mail. Scanner clusters label on-premises files and have nothing to do with email.

prompt: A company's policy intent statement says: "Prevent users from emailing credit card numbers to recipients outside the organization." Which DLP rule configuration maps to this intent for the Exchange location?

options.text: Content contains the Credit Card Number sensitive information type OR content is shared with people outside my organization
Content contains the Credit Card Number sensitive information type AND content is shared with people outside my organization
Content contains any sensitivity label AND the sender is a member of the Finance group
Content is shared with people inside my organization, with an exception for credit card numbers

explanation: The intent needs both conditions to be true: the message contains credit card numbers and it is shared with people outside the organization, so the conditions are joined with AND. Joining them with OR would act on every external email and on internal email with card numbers. A sensitivity label condition scoped to Finance doesn't detect credit card numbers. Matching internal sharing with a card-number exception does the opposite of the intent.

prompt: A DLP policy for SharePoint and OneDrive has been reviewed and approved by stakeholders. The team wants to measure how often it would match and tune it before any user is affected or notified. Which policy state should the administrator choose next?

options.text: Run the policy in simulation mode with policy tips
Turn it on right away
Run the policy in simulation mode
Keep it off

explanation: Simulation mode enforces no actions and audits events, so you can monitor the policy's impact in the simulation overview and Activity explorer without affecting or notifying users. Simulation with policy tips shows tips and notifications to users. Turning the policy on enforces its actions. Keeping it off makes the policy inactive, so it collects no data.

prompt: A DLP policy blocks sharing of documents that contain customer account numbers. The team suspects some matches are false positives and wants users to be able to continue when they have a legitimate need, while recording their reason so the policy can be tuned. Which action should the rule use?

options.text: Audit only, with a notification to users
Allow, with auditing turned on
Block, with an incident report
Block with override

explanation: Block with override blocks the activity by default but lets users override it and provide a reason, which gives direct feedback for identifying false positives. Audit only allows the activity with no block. Allow is only available for the Devices location and doesn't block anything. Block prevents the activity no matter what, so users with a legitimate need can't continue.

prompt: A company is deploying a new DLP policy for SharePoint and OneDrive. It wants to start with the least impactful action that still produces audit data and can send notifications to users. Which action should the administrator configure first?

options.text: Audit only
Allow
Block with override
Block

explanation: Audit only lets the user activity occur while producing audit data, and you can add notifications and alerts; it is the least impactful action for locations other than Devices. Allow is available only for policies scoped to the Devices location. Block with override and Block both interrupt business processes.

prompt: A security analyst must create and manage DLP policies in the Microsoft Purview portal. Following least privilege, the analyst shouldn't receive permissions for other compliance solutions. What should the administrator assign?

options.text: The Global Administrator role
The Compliance administrator role group
A role group that contains the DLP Compliance Management role
The Information Protection Readers role group in Microsoft Purview

explanation: A role group that contains the DLP Compliance Management role grants the permissions needed to manage DLP policies without unrelated solutions. Global Administrator and Compliance administrator can create DLP policies but grant far broader permissions. Information Protection Readers provides read-only access and can't create policies.

prompt: An auditor must be able to view DLP policy configurations in the Microsoft Purview portal but must not be able to create, edit, or delete them. Which role should the auditor be given?

options.text: View-only DLP compliance management
The DLP Compliance Management role
Compliance Data administrator role group
Information Protection Admin

explanation: View-only DLP compliance management provides read-only access to DLP policies. DLP Compliance Management allows creating and editing policies. Compliance Data administrator and Information Protection Admin both include permissions to create and modify policies, so they exceed the read-only requirement.

prompt: A company wants to stop users from sharing SharePoint and OneDrive files that contain passport numbers with external users, while employees inside the organization keep their access. Which DLP action should the rule use?

options.text: Restrict access or encrypt the content, and block everyone
Restrict access or encrypt the content, and block only people outside your organization
Audit or restrict activities on devices, and block copying files to removable USB devices
Add an HTML disclaimer to the content and notify the user who last modified it

explanation: Blocking only people outside your organization removes external access while internal users keep theirs. Blocking everyone leaves access only to the content owner, the last modifier, and the site admin, which would cut off other employees. Device activity restrictions apply to the Devices location, not to sharing in SharePoint and OneDrive. An HTML disclaimer is an Exchange action and doesn't restrict file access.

prompt: An Exchange DLP policy is scoped to include only the Finance distribution group. A user in HR sends an email with bank account numbers to a member of Finance, and the policy takes no action. Why?

options.text: Exchange DLP policies only evaluate email sent outside the organization
Exchange DLP policies don't support distribution groups for scoping
The policy must be in simulation mode to evaluate internal email
Scope is based on the sender, and the HR sender isn't in scope

explanation: For Exchange, the policy applies when the sender is in scope; if the sender is out of scope but the recipient is in scope, the policy doesn't apply. Exchange DLP policies can evaluate internal email, depending on the conditions. Distribution groups are supported for Exchange scoping, with up to 50 inclusions and exclusions per policy. Simulation mode doesn't change scoping and enforces no actions.

prompt: A DLP rule must match items that either contain U.S. passport numbers or have the Confidential sensitivity label. How should the administrator configure the Content contains condition?

options.text: Add the passport sensitive information type and the Confidential label in one group, joined with Any of these
Add the passport sensitive information type and the Confidential label in one group, joined with All of these
Add the Confidential label as an exception to a passport condition
Create two separate DLP policies, because one condition can't contain both types

explanation: The Content contains condition supports sensitive information types and sensitivity labels together, and joining them with Any of these is an OR, so either one matches. All of these is an AND and would require both. An exception would exclude labeled items instead of including them. Two policies aren't needed, because one condition can include both.

prompt: A company wants a DLP rule to generate a high-severity alert only when a single email contains 10 or more credit card numbers. Emails with fewer numbers should be handled by a separate low-severity rule. What should the administrator configure in the high-severity rule?

options.text: Increase the confidence level of the Credit Card Number type to High
Add a condition that the message size is greater than 10 KB
Set the instance count for the Credit Card Number type to a minimum of 10
