prompt: Investigators need audit records of the search queries that a licensed Audit (Premium) user runs in Outlook against their mailbox. These records do not appear in audit searches. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Create an audit log retention policy for the Exchange record type
Assign the user the View-Only Audit Logs role
Run Set-Mailbox for the user with -AuditOwner @{Add="SearchQueryInitiated"}
Turn on SearchQueryInitiatedSharePoint in the Microsoft Purview portal

explanation: The SearchQueryInitiatedExchange event must be explicitly enabled per user by adding SearchQueryInitiated to the AuditOwner actions with Set-Mailbox in Exchange Online PowerShell. A retention policy only controls how long existing records are kept. The View-Only Audit Logs role lets someone search the log; it does not create records. SharePoint search logging is already enabled by default and does not cover Exchange searches.

prompt: An internal investigator must be able to search and export the audit log but must not be able to turn audit logging on or off. Which role group should the investigator be added to?

options.text: Audit Manager
Audit Reader
Compliance Data Administrator
Organization Management

explanation: Members of the Audit Reader role group get the View-Only Audit Logs role and can only search and export the audit log. Audit Manager also grants the Audit Logs role, which can change audit settings such as enabling or disabling logging. Compliance Data Administrator and Organization Management grant much broader permissions than needed.

prompt: An administrator wants to create an audit log retention policy in the Microsoft Purview portal but the option to create a policy is not available. Which role does the administrator need?

options.text: Audit Logs
Retention Management
Organization Configuration
View-Only Audit Logs

explanation: The Organization Configuration role is required to create or modify an audit log retention policy. Audit Logs and View-Only Audit Logs relate to searching the audit log and audit settings, not creating retention policies for audit records. Retention Management applies to retention policies and labels for content, not audit records.

prompt: An organization uses Audit (Premium) and has not created any audit log retention policies. For a user with a Microsoft 365 E5 license, how long are SharePoint audit records and Microsoft Teams audit records retained?

options.text: Both are retained for 180 days
SharePoint records for one year, and Teams records for 180 days
Both are retained for one year
SharePoint records for 10 years, and Teams records for one year

explanation: The default Audit (Premium) policy retains Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive and Microsoft Entra records for one year for E5-licensed users; records from other workloads, such as Teams, are retained for 180 days unless a custom policy changes it. Nothing is retained for 10 years without a custom policy and the 10-year add-on licence.

prompt: A regulator requires that audit records for all Microsoft Teams activities be kept for 10 years. Users have Microsoft 365 E5 licenses. What must the organization do?

options.text: Create a 10-year audit log retention policy for Teams and assign the 10-year retention add-on
Create a data lifecycle retention policy that keeps Teams chats for 10 years
Export the audit log every 180 days and store it in a SharePoint library
Place all users' mailboxes on eDiscovery hold for 10 years

explanation: Audit records can be kept for up to 10 years with an audit log retention policy, but the users who generate the records must also have the 10-Year Audit Log Retention add-on in addition to E5. Data lifecycle retention policies keep Teams messages, not audit records. Manually exporting is not a supported retention method, and an eDiscovery hold preserves mailbox content, not the audit log.

prompt: Two audit log retention policies match the same Exchange mailbox activity for a user. Policy A has priority 10 and retains records for one year. Policy B has priority 100 and retains records for 30 days. How long are the records kept?

options.text: 30 days, because the shortest duration wins
One year, because policy A has the higher priority
One year, because the longest duration always wins
30 days, because policy B was created last

explanation: Audit log retention policies are processed by priority, and a lower value means a higher priority, so policy A with priority 10 is applied. Audit retention does not use longest or shortest duration rules like content retention, and creation order does not matter.

prompt: An administrator needs an audit log retention policy for a record type that is not offered in the Create audit retention policy page of the Microsoft Purview portal. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Use New-UnifiedAuditLogRetentionPolicy in Security & Compliance PowerShell
Use Set-Mailbox with the AuditLogAgeLimit parameter
Create a retention label for the record type
Open a support request to add the record type to the portal

explanation: New-UnifiedAuditLogRetentionPolicy in Security & Compliance PowerShell can create policies for record types or activities that the portal does not offer; such policies must then be edited with Set-UnifiedAuditLogRetentionPolicy. AuditLogAgeLimit applies to mailbox audit logging settings, not unified audit retention policies. Retention labels apply to content, not audit records, and no support request is needed.

prompt: A tenant has users with Microsoft 365 E5 licenses and contractors with Microsoft 365 E3 licenses. A custom audit log retention policy retains all SharePoint activity for one year for all users. How long are SharePoint audit records retained for activities performed by the contractors?

options.text: One year, because the policy applies to all users
90 days, the original Audit (Standard) default
Indefinitely, until the retention policy is deleted
180 days, because the contractors lack E5 licensing

explanation: Retaining audit records longer than 180 days requires the user who generates the record to have an E5 or qualifying add-on licence; records for users without it are kept for 180 days. The policy cannot extend retention beyond what the user's licence supports. The 90-day default applied only to Audit (Standard) logs generated before October 17, 2023, and no audit policy retains records indefinitely.

prompt: A compliance officer opens Activity explorer to review label downgrades from five weeks ago but cannot find them. What is the most likely reason, and what should the officer use instead?

options.text: Activity explorer shows only Endpoint DLP events; use Content explorer
The events need the Audit (Premium) licence; use Policy lookup
Activity explorer reports on up to 30 days of data; search the audit log instead
Label events take five weeks to appear; wait and refresh Activity explorer

explanation: Activity explorer reports on up to 30 days of data from the unified audit log, so older label events should be found with an audit log search. Activity explorer includes label, DLP and endpoint events, not just Endpoint DLP. Content explorer shows where labeled items are, not past activities. Policy lookup finds retention policies, and core service events usually appear within 60 to 90 minutes.

prompt: An information protection team suspects that users are downgrading documents from Highly Confidential to General. Which tool lets them quickly filter these events by user and location for the past few weeks?

options.text: Content explorer, filtered by the General label
Activity explorer, with the label changes filter set
Data explorer, filtered by sensitive information type
The Adaptive Protection dashboard in Insider Risk Management

explanation: Activity explorer provides a historical view of actions on labeled content and includes a predefined filter set for sensitivity labels applied, changed or removed, with filters such as user and location. Content explorer shows current items and their labels, not the change history. Data explorer summarises classification counts. The Adaptive Protection dashboard shows users' insider risk levels.

prompt: An administrator turns on a new DLP policy and immediately opens Activity explorer, which shows no DLP rule matches for Exchange. Ten minutes later it is still empty. What is the most likely explanation?

options.text: The policy failed to deploy and must be recreated
Activity explorer shows only Endpoint DLP device events
Its data comes from the audit log, which takes 60 to 90 minutes
Exchange DLP events are shown only in Content explorer

explanation: Activity explorer isn't real time; its data comes from the unified audit log, and core services such as Exchange usually take 60 to 90 minutes, plus time for the policy to reach the workload. An empty view right after turning on a policy usually doesn't mean the policy failed. Activity explorer includes Exchange DLP matches, and Content explorer doesn't list DLP events.

prompt: A company with Microsoft 365 E3 licenses and no add-ons wants a DLP alert to be raised only when 50 or more emails containing customer data are sent externally within 24 hours. What is required?

options.text: Configure the alert to be raised every time a rule matches
Turn on user and rule based alert aggregation for the tenant
Change the rule severity to High
An E5 subscription, or a qualifying add-on to E3

explanation: Threshold-based aggregated alerts require an A5, E5 or G5 subscription, or an E1, F1, G1, E3 or G3 subscription with a qualifying add-on such as Microsoft Purview Suite or the eDiscovery and Audit add-on. Alerting on every match does not use a threshold. User and rule based aggregation groups single-event alerts by user in short time windows. Severity does not create volume thresholds.

prompt: A DLP analyst can open alerts in the DLP alerts dashboard but cannot see the matched sensitive content or content preview for the items. The analyst should be able to see this content. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Add the analyst to the Content Explorer Content Viewer role group
Add the analyst to the Audit Reader role group
Assign the analyst the View-Only DLP Compliance Management role
Assign the analyst the Insider Risk Management Analysts role group

explanation: Content preview and the matched sensitive content and context features in DLP alerts require membership of the Content Explorer Content Viewer role group, which has the Data classification content viewer role. Audit Reader is for audit log search. View-Only DLP Compliance Management provides dashboard access, which the analyst already has. Insider Risk Management roles do not grant DLP content preview.

prompt: A security operations team wants to investigate DLP alerts together with related Defender for Endpoint and Defender for Office 365 alerts for the same user in one place. Which portal does Microsoft recommend for investigating and managing DLP alerts?

options.text: The Policies page of DLP in the Microsoft Purview portal
The incidents queue in the Microsoft Defender portal
The Microsoft Entra admin center sign-in logs
The Exchange admin center message trace

explanation: Microsoft recommends the Microsoft Defender XDR portal for investigating and managing DLP alerts, where they can be correlated with alerts from other Defender products in incidents; the Purview portal is the recommended place to create and edit DLP policies. Entra sign-in logs and Exchange message trace show sign-in and mail flow data but do not manage DLP alerts.

prompt: An administrator changes the alert settings in an existing DLP rule so that alerts are sent at High severity. After 30 minutes, no new alerts appear for matching activity. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Recreate the policy because alert settings cannot be changed
Turn off the policy and turn it back on
Assign Audit (Premium) licenses to the users in scope
Wait, because alert changes can take up to 3 hours to start generating alerts

explanation: It can take up to 3 hours to start generating alerts after alerts are configured or modified in a DLP policy, so waiting is the correct action. Alert settings can be edited in an existing rule. Toggling the policy does not speed things up, and Audit (Premium) licences are not required for DLP alerts.

prompt: DLP alerts from several months ago are no longer visible in the alerts dashboard, and the compliance team wants to keep them visible longer. Which setting controls how long DLP alerts remain visible?

options.text: The retention policy for the Exchange mailboxes location
The DLP policy's incident report settings
The Activity explorer data range
The organization's audit log retention policies

explanation: The organization's audit log retention policy configuration controls how long a DLP alert remains visible in the console. Content retention policies apply to mailbox content, incident reports set who gets notified and at what severity, and the Activity explorer range is a reporting window, not an alert retention setting.

prompt: An insider risk investigator needs to review the recent activities of an employee who has no insider risk alerts, at the request of HR. Which Insider Risk Management feature should the investigator use?

options.text: User activity reports in Insider Risk Management
The Adaptive Protection dashboard
Analytics insights on the Overview page
Forensic evidence policies

explanation: User activity reports let investigators review the activities of a specific user over a period even when the user has no alerts or policy matches. The Adaptive Protection dashboard summarises users with insider risk levels. Analytics provides aggregated tenant insights, not one user's activity. Forensic evidence policies define what to capture and require approved capture requests.

prompt: A Defender for Cloud Apps file policy alert reports a SharePoint file containing payroll data shared with external users. Investigators want the file removed from all access and moved to a location where an administrator must review it before it is released. Which governance action should be used?

options.text: Put in user quarantine
Notify file owner
Remove external users
Put in admin quarantine

explanation: Put in admin quarantine removes all permissions from the file and moves it to a quarantine folder in an administrator location so an admin can review and release or remove it. User quarantine moves the file to a folder under the user's own drive so the user can review it. Notifying the owner does not restrict access. Removing external users keeps internal access.

prompt: A file policy in Defender for Cloud Apps finds OneDrive files containing source code that are shared with people outside the company. The owners must keep working on the files with internal colleagues. Which governance action is most appropriate?

options.text: Make private
Remove external users
Trash
Put in admin quarantine

explanation: Remove external users removes all collaborators outside the domains configured as internal while keeping internal sharing in place. Make private removes all shares so only site admins can access the file. Trash moves the file to the recycle bin, and admin quarantine removes all permissions; both would stop the owners working with colleagues.

prompt: An administrator applied a governance action from a Defender for Cloud Apps file policy alert and needs to confirm whether it succeeded, and revert it if necessary. Where should the administrator look?

options.text: Activity explorer in the Microsoft Purview portal
An audit log search in the Microsoft Purview portal
The Governance log for Cloud Apps in the Defender portal
The incidents queue in Microsoft Sentinel

explanation: The Governance log under Cloud Apps in the Microsoft Defender portal records the status of each governance task, shows success or failure, and lets you retry or revert some actions. Activity explorer and the audit log show user and admin activities but cannot revert Defender for Cloud Apps actions. Sentinel incidents do not track governance task status.

prompt: Two Defender for Cloud Apps file policies match the same SharePoint file. One policy applies Remove external users, and the other applies Make private. What is the result?

options.text: Only the policy that was created first is applied
Both actions fail because they conflict
The file is put in admin quarantine instead
The stronger action, Make private, is enforced

explanation: When one governance action is contained in another, such as Remove external users within Make private, Defender for Cloud Apps resolves the conflict by enforcing the stronger action. Policy creation order does not decide the outcome, contained actions do not cause failure, and quarantine is not substituted automatically.

prompt: A legal team needs to find all email and documents that mention a project code name across specific custodians' mailboxes and OneDrive accounts, and then review the results with tagging. What should the eDiscovery manager do?

options.text: Search in an eDiscovery case and add the results to a review set
Run a Content explorer query for the code name and export it
Use Activity explorer to find items that mention the code name
Auto-apply a retention label that uses the code name as a keyword

explanation: In eDiscovery you create a case, create a search in the case with the relevant data sources and query, and add the results to a review set, where items can be searched, filtered and tagged. Content explorer and Activity explorer show classified items and activities, not keyword searches with review. A retention label policy applies labels and does not provide a review workflow.

prompt: A company has many eDiscovery cases. A compliance lead must be able to access and manage every case in the organization, including cases where they are not a member. Which role group should the lead be added to?

options.text: eDiscovery Manager role group, as an eDiscovery Manager
Records Management role group
eDiscovery Manager role group, as an eDiscovery Administrator
Audit Manager role group

explanation: eDiscovery Administrators, a subgroup of the eDiscovery Manager role group, can access all eDiscovery cases in the organization. eDiscovery Managers can access only cases that they create or are members of. Records Management and Audit Manager do not grant access to eDiscovery cases.

prompt: During an eDiscovery investigation, a reviewer wants to see a short list of actual items returned by a search to check whether the query is accurate before exporting anything. The search currently shows only statistics. What should the reviewer do?

options.text: Add all of the search results to a review set
Generate sample results on the Sample tab
Create an eDiscovery hold for the data sources
Download the search reports as a .csv file

explanation: On the Sample tab, the reviewer can select Generate sample results and run the query to view a sample of items and evaluate the query. Adding everything to a review set is more than needed for a quick check. A hold preserves content and does not display results. The downloaded reports give summary information rather than a preview of the items.

prompt: A company is rolling out Microsoft 365 Copilot. Files and emails labeled Highly Confidential must not be summarized by Copilot or agents, whether or not they are encrypted, but users must still be able to open them normally. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: A DLP policy for the Microsoft 365 Copilot location that targets the label
A retention policy that covers the Microsoft Copilot experiences location
An Insider Risk Management policy from the Risky AI usage template
A communication compliance policy that reviews Copilot interactions

explanation: A DLP policy for the Microsoft 365 Copilot location can stop Copilot and agents from processing items with selected sensitivity labels, encrypted or not; Copilot can still reference them with a link and users can open them directly. A retention policy controls how long prompts and responses are kept. Insider risk and communication compliance policies detect and score risky behaviour but do not stop Copilot from summarizing content.

prompt: A sensitivity label applies encryption that grants recipients the VIEW right only. What happens when a user who has this right asks Microsoft 365 Copilot about a document protected by the label?

options.text: Copilot summarizes the document because the user can view it
Copilot removes the label before summarizing the document
Copilot does not summarize the content but can reference it with a link
Copilot summarizes the document only in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat

explanation: Copilot honors the EXTRACT usage right; if the user has VIEW but not EXTRACT, Copilot won't summarize the content but can reference it with a link so the user can open it outside Copilot. Viewing rights alone are not enough to return text. Copilot never removes labels, and the restriction applies across Copilot experiences.

prompt: An administrator is designing a sensitivity label with encryption for project documents that Copilot must be able to summarize for authorized users. Which usage right must the permissions include?

options.text: FORWARD
PRINT
EXPORT
EXTRACT

explanation: EXTRACT, shown in the portal as Copy and extract content, decides whether Copilot and agents can display text from encrypted content to the user; Full control (OWNER) includes it automatically. FORWARD controls forwarding email, PRINT controls printing, and EXPORT relates to saving in other formats and changing labels; none of them lets Copilot return text.

prompt: A research division protects its most sensitive files with Double Key Encryption (DKE). How does Microsoft 365 Copilot handle these files?

options.text: Copilot summarizes them, but only for the file owner
Copilot can't access them, even when they are open in an app
Copilot can access them if the user has the EXTRACT right
Copilot can access them once a Copilot DLP policy allows it

explanation: Because DKE is intended for the most sensitive data, Copilot and agents can't access it: DKE items are not returned by Copilot, and Copilot can't be used in the app while a DKE item is open. EXTRACT rights or DLP settings do not change this, and there is no owner exception.

prompt: Regulations require that users' prompts and Copilot responses in Microsoft 365 Copilot be kept for three years and then deleted. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: A retention label published to all users' OneDrive accounts
An audit log retention policy for Copilot record types
A retention policy that includes the Microsoft Copilot experiences location
An eDiscovery hold on every user's mailbox

explanation: Retention policies support the Microsoft Copilot experiences location to retain and delete Copilot interactions, which are stored in the SubstrateHolds folder in the mailbox. Retention labels are not supported for Copilot interactions. An audit retention policy keeps audit records, which do not include the prompt or response text. An eDiscovery hold keeps data but doesn't delete it after three years.

prompt: During a legal investigation, counsel needs the actual text of prompts that an employee sent to Microsoft 365 Copilot and the responses returned. An audit log search shows Copilot interaction records but not the text. What should the investigator use?

options.text: Content explorer, filtered by the employee's name
Audit (Premium) intelligent insights for the employee
A Defender for Cloud Apps activity policy
eDiscovery, searching the employee's Copilot data

explanation: Auditing captures Copilot activity but not the actual prompt or response; Microsoft directs you to eDiscovery, or to the AI interaction events in DSPM for AI Activity explorer, for the text. Content explorer shows classified items, not Copilot conversations. Audit (Premium) insights still don't include prompt text. Defender for Cloud Apps activity policies don't collect Copilot conversations.

prompt: A security team wants DSPM for AI to show when users paste credit card numbers into third-party generative AI websites from Windows devices using Google Chrome. Which two prerequisites must be in place? (Choose two.)

options.text: The devices are onboarded to Microsoft Purview
The Microsoft Purview browser extension is deployed to Chrome on the devices
Users are assigned Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses
An Audit (Premium) retention policy for AI record types exists
The devices run the Microsoft Purview Information Protection client

explanation: Visibility into sensitive information shared with third-party AI sites requires devices onboarded to Microsoft Purview, and on Windows with Chrome the Microsoft Purview browser extension is also needed. Copilot licences are needed only to monitor Microsoft 365 Copilot. Audit retention policies control how long audit records are kept, and the Information Protection client is for labeling files.

prompt: A company wants DSPM for AI to monitor interactions and apply DLP policies to unmanaged generative AI apps used in Microsoft Edge, without relying on device onboarding. What must the administrator configure?

options.text: An Edge policy that turns on the Purview integration in Edge
Restricted Content Discovery for all of the SharePoint sites
A Defender for Cloud Apps session policy for each AI app
A collection policy for Copilot in Microsoft Fabric

explanation: Monitoring interactions and applying DLP policies to other AI apps in Edge requires an Edge configuration policy to activate the Microsoft Purview integration in Edge. Restricted Content Discovery limits what Copilot can discover in SharePoint. Session policies in Defender for Cloud Apps are a different control and aren't the DSPM for AI prerequisite. A collection policy for Copilot in Fabric applies to Fabric, not Edge.

prompt: DSPM for AI reports show interactions with Microsoft 365 Copilot but nothing for enterprise AI apps such as ChatGPT Enterprise. The portal displays a billing notification. What is most likely missing?

options.text: A Microsoft 365 Copilot licence for each user
Pay-as-you-go billing for the organization
The Insider Risk Management Admins role for the administrator
An adaptive scope for AI users

explanation: For AI apps other than Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft Facilitator, pay-as-you-go billing must be set up for the organization, and the portal shows notifications when it applies. Copilot licences enable Microsoft 365 Copilot monitoring, which already works. Insider Risk Management roles and adaptive scopes do not enable data collection from other AI apps.

prompt: A new DSPM for AI deployment shows no Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions even though licensed users are using Copilot. Which prerequisite should the administrator verify first?

options.text: That Endpoint DLP just-in-time protection is enabled
That a SASE integration is configured in DLP settings
That Microsoft Purview auditing is turned on for the organization
That the Defender for Endpoint integration is enabled

explanation: Monitoring interactions with Microsoft 365 Copilot and agents requires Microsoft Purview auditing to be enabled, along with Copilot licences for users. Just-in-time protection is an Endpoint DLP feature, SASE integrations support network-based detection for other AI apps, and Defender for Endpoint integration is used by insider risk security policy templates.

prompt: A data security analyst must be able to view DSPM for AI reports, recommendations and policies, but must not create or change anything. Which role or role group should the analyst get with the least privilege?

options.text: Microsoft Purview Compliance Administrator role group
Microsoft Entra Compliance Administrator role
Purview Data Security AI Viewer role
Insider Risk Management Admins role group

explanation: The Purview Data Security AI Viewer role provides view-only access to DSPM for AI, as does the Security Reader role group. The Purview Compliance Administrator role group and the Entra Compliance Administrator role can view, create and edit. Insider Risk Management Admins configure insider risk policies and don't give a read-only DSPM for AI view.

prompt: A compliance administrator who is a member of the Microsoft Purview Compliance Administrator role group can see AI interaction events in DSPM for AI Activity explorer, but the prompt and response text is not shown. What additional role should be assigned?

options.text: Purview Data Security AI Content Viewer
Purview Data Security AI Viewer
Audit Reader
eDiscovery Manager

explanation: Viewing the prompts and responses inside AI interaction events requires the Purview Data Security AI Content Viewer role or the Content Explorer Content Viewer role group; the compliance administrator roles alone do not include it. Data Security AI Viewer gives view-only access without content. Audit Reader is for audit log searches, and eDiscovery Manager is for cases.

prompt: An analyst using DSPM for AI Activity explorer wants to see the insider risk level of the users who appear in AI events and follow a link to their details in Insider Risk Management. What should the analyst be granted?

options.text: The Microsoft Entra Global Administrator role in the tenant
The Insider Risk Management Investigators role group
The Purview Data Security AI Content Viewer role
The Microsoft Purview Security Reader role group

explanation: Viewing an individual user's risk level and the link to user details in DSPM for AI Activity explorer requires the Insider Risk Management Analysts or Investigators role groups; even Global Administrator and compliance administrator roles do not include this. The AI Content Viewer role shows prompt text, and Security Reader is a view-only DSPM role without insider risk data.

prompt: A company uses administrative units. A regional compliance administrator who is assigned an administrative unit tries to create the one-click DSPM for AI policies that apply to all users, but cannot. What is the reason?

options.text: One-click policies require the Data Security AI Viewer role
One-click policies can be created only by Global Administrators
One-click policies are disabled when administrative units exist
Restricted administrators can't create all-user one-click policies

explanation: When administrative units are used, restricted administrators can't create one-click policies that apply to all users; an unrestricted administrator must create them. The AI Viewer role is read-only. Compliance administrators who are unrestricted can also create them, so Global Administrator is not required, and administrative units do not disable the policies for everyone.

prompt: A company wants to start by discovering which sensitive information users paste or upload into AI websites in Edge, Chrome and Firefox, without blocking anyone yet. Which DSPM for AI one-click policy meets this goal?

options.text: DSPM for AI - Block sensitive info from AI sites
DSPM for AI - Protect sensitive data from Copilot processing
DSPM for AI: Detect sensitive info added to AI sites
DSPM for AI - Unethical behavior in AI apps

explanation: The DLP policy DSPM for AI: Detect sensitive info added to AI sites discovers sensitive content pasted or uploaded to AI sites in Edge, Chrome and Firefox, for all users, in audit mode only. Block sensitive info from AI sites uses Adaptive Protection to block with override. Protect sensitive data from Copilot processing stops Copilot processing labeled items. Unethical behavior in AI apps is a communication compliance policy.

prompt: A company wants users who Adaptive Protection identifies as elevated risk to be blocked, with an option to override, when they paste or upload sensitive information to AI apps in Edge, Chrome and Firefox. Other users must not be affected. Which DSPM for AI recommendation policy should the administrator create?

options.text: DSPM for AI - Block sensitive info from AI sites
DSPM for AI - Detect when users visit AI sites
DSPM for AI - Capture interactions for enterprise AI apps
DSPM for AI - Detect risky AI usage

explanation: DSPM for AI - Block sensitive info from AI sites is a DLP policy that uses Adaptive Protection to apply block with override to elevated risk users who paste or upload sensitive information to AI apps; it starts in test mode. Detect when users visit AI sites and Detect risky AI usage are insider risk policies that detect activity. Capture interactions for enterprise AI apps is a collection policy for capturing prompts and responses.

prompt: An ethics committee wants to detect harassing or threatening language and sensitive information in the prompts and responses users exchange with Microsoft 365 Copilot and other AI apps. Which solution does the DSPM for AI one-click policy for this scenario use?

options.text: Data loss prevention
Insider Risk Management
Communication Compliance
Data lifecycle management

explanation: The recommendation Detect unethical behavior in AI apps creates the Communication Compliance policy DSPM for AI - Unethical behavior in AI apps, which reviews prompts and responses. DLP prevents sharing of sensitive data, Insider Risk Management scores users' risky activities, and data lifecycle management retains or deletes content.

prompt: An organization wants to capture prompts and responses from ChatGPT Enterprise so they can be searched in eDiscovery and kept by data lifecycle management. Which type of policy does DSPM for AI create for this?

options.text: A DLP policy for the Devices location
A collection policy
An auto-apply retention label policy
An Insider Risk Management policy

explanation: The DSPM for AI - Capture interactions for enterprise AI apps policy is a collection policy that captures prompts and responses from enterprise AI apps, such as ChatGPT Enterprise, for eDiscovery and data lifecycle management. Device DLP policies detect and restrict sharing but don't capture conversations. Auto-apply retention labels label existing content. Insider risk policies score user activity.

prompt: A company routes all web traffic through a Secure Service Edge (SSE) provider and wants DSPM for AI to detect sensitive information shared with AI apps through browsers, APIs and add-ins. Which step is required before the related one-click collection policy can detect these interactions?

options.text: Install the Microsoft Purview browser extension on all devices
Enable Restricted SharePoint Search
Create an adaptive scope for users of the SSE provider
Add the SASE or SSE integration in Data Loss Prevention settings

explanation: The DSPM for AI - Detect sensitive info shared with AI via network policy requires one or more SASE or SSE integrations to be added manually in Data Loss Prevention settings, and detection depends on the network partner. The browser extension supports browser-based detection on devices, not network detection. Restricted SharePoint Search limits Copilot and search to selected sites. Adaptive scopes do not connect a network provider.

prompt: The DSPM for AI collection policy for network-based detection is creating events, but administrators see no prompt or response text in the AI interaction events. What should the administrator do?

Turn on Always audit file activity for devices

Edit the collection policy and select the option to capture content

DLP rule match
Sensitive info types

prompt: A compliance team wants DSPM for AI to report when sensitive information types appear in Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions. They have not created any DLP or insider risk policies yet. Which statement is correct?

A communication compliance policy must be created first
Sensitive info type events require pay-as-you-go billing for Copilot
With auditing on, these events are recorded without any policies

prompt: Before rolling out Microsoft 365 Copilot, the HR department's SharePoint sites are under a permissions review. Content from these sites must not appear in Copilot responses or organization-wide search, but HR staff must keep their access to the sites. What should the SharePoint administrator configure?

options.text: Remove all members from the HR sites until the review is complete
Turn on Restricted Content Discovery for the HR sites
Apply a retention policy to the HR sites
Apply a sensitivity label with Do Not Forward to the HR sites

explanation: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting that stops a site's content from appearing in organization-wide search and Copilot responses without changing permissions, so users with access can keep working. Removing members blocks access entirely. Retention policies keep or delete content but don't affect discovery. Do Not Forward is an email protection option, and site container labels don't prevent Copilot from discovering items.

prompt: A user asks Microsoft 365 Copilot to create a new document from two source files: one labeled General and one labeled Confidential, where Confidential has the higher priority. The new document has no label. What label does Copilot apply through sensitivity label inheritance?

options.text: General, because it is applied first
No label, because inheritance applies only to emails
The default label from the user's label policy
Confidential, because it has the higher priority

explanation: With sensitivity label inheritance, content Copilot creates from labeled items inherits the highest priority label, so Confidential is applied. Label order of the sources doesn't matter, inheritance isn't limited to email, and an inherited label takes the place of a lower-priority default label.

prompt: A Microsoft Teams team is labeled Confidential through the container label settings for groups and sites. An administrator expects Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat to display the Confidential label when it summarizes that team's channel messages. What actually happens?

Copilot refuses to summarize any content from labeled teams
Copilot doesn't show it, because items don't inherit container labels
Copilot applies the container label to the summarized messages

explanation: Sensitivity labels applied to containers such as Teams, Microsoft 365 Groups and SharePoint sites aren't inherited by the items in those containers, so summarized channel messages don't show the container label in Copilot and can't support label inheritance. Container labels don't block Copilot from summarizing, and Copilot doesn't apply container labels to messages.
